chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ali ibn al-Hasan, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them both), who said:

I asked him about a man who married off his slave girl to his brother, or his paternal uncle, or his cousin, or his nephew, and she bore a child; what is the status of the child? He said: 'If the child inherits from whoever owned him (the father) a portion, he becomes free.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: And all those whom we mentioned regarding the fact that their ownership is not valid due to lineage, likewise their ownership is not valid due to breastfeeding. This is indicated by what we have previously mentioned from the narrations regarding that which is prohibited due to breastfeeding is prohibited due to lineage, and that is general for all rulings. And this is also indicated by what was narrated:
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the freedom of a child born to a slave girl married to a relative?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam Musa al-Kadhim (AS), the legal principle of 'walad al-ribah' (child of concubinage) is clarified: emancipation is contingent upon the child's right to inherit from the master, establishing a direct link between lineage rights and freedom. Shaykh al-Tusi further elucidates that the prohibitions arising from breastfeeding (radāʿ) are comprehensive, mirroring those of lineage across all categories of marriage and inheritance, a concept rooted in the general Quranic verse regarding nursing kinship.
